request.rationale: Online pH and oxygen are stable, but the 26 h metabolic sample is old. Request a current valid panel before deciding whether perfusion should change.

The valid 48 h sample shows increasing cell density and lactate with independent pH matching the online channel. Increase dilution to 6 mL/h and reassess at 60 h, without assigning an unsupported fault.
Reassess the effect of increased perfusion after ten hours; no instrument fault is established.
Independent pH, viability and glucose remain acceptable within the illustrative model. Maintain 6 mL/h and schedule another metabolic assessment.
Obtain current glucose and lactate rather than continuing to control from a fourteen-hour-old sample.
Lactate is approaching 2 g/L as biomass rises. Increase dilution to 10 mL/h; the ample medium budget supports this action, though its cost must be reported.
Update the current metabolic state after twenty hours and plan the qualifying banking samples after the 114 h checkpoint.
Lactate has reached 2.037 g/L with continued growth. Increase dilution within the permitted range and plan near-endpoint QC collection at 118 h rather than relying on an earlier checkpoint.
Obtain current metabolism and the complete stage-specific banking evidence at the qualified 118 h collection time. Do not infer genomic or microbial quality from normal telemetry.
Near-endpoint viability and independent pH are available, but four required QC channels are pending. Advance the evidence clock without further culture interventions.
